items.description: Deep analysis of repository structure, tooling, and agent orchestration pipeline
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase1/repo_analysis.md documenting: (a) all modules (.archivara/, .opencode/, tools), (b) agent roles and permissions, (c) concept_evolve workflow and output structure under results/concept_evolve/tree/, (d) semantic_scholar CLI usage patterns. Must reference at least 5 specific files with line numbers.

items.description: Conduct comprehensive web-based literature search on univalent Bloch constant bounds (B_u)
items.acceptance_criteria: Using web search and Semantic Scholar tools, identify and document at least 15 relevant papers. Must include: Skinner 2009, Beller-Hummel 1985, Carroll-Ortega-Cerda 2008, Bhowmik-Sen 2023, Yanagihara 1995, Bonk 1990, Chen-Gauthier 1996, Ahlfors-Grunsky 1937, Baernstein-Vinson 2000, Goodman 1945, Kudryavtseva-Solodov 2022, Eremenko 2011, Chen-Shiba 2004, Roth 2002, and at least 1 paper from 2023-2026. Record all in sources.bib at repo root with complete BibTeX entries.

items.description: Analyze Skinner's 2009 lower bound proof technique in detail
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase1/skinner_analysis.md with: (a) the precise statement B_u > 0.5708858, (b) the bootstrapping method from Koebe distortion, (c) the implicit function C(|z|) >= B(|z|) that upgrades the growth bound, (d) identification of where the proof loses tightness and what inequalities are non-sharp. At least 3 specific weaknesses or slack points must be identified.

items.description: Analyze Carroll-Ortega-Cerda upper bound approach and the extremal domain structure
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase1/upper_bound_analysis.md documenting: (a) the Goodman domain modification, (b) Polya-Chebotarev problem and Fedorov's solution, (c) harmonic symmetry and conformal welding techniques, (d) the numerical upper bound ~0.6564 for univalent Bloch-Landau constant, (e) relationship between B_u upper bound and L upper bound. Must cite Carroll 2008 and Carroll-Ortega-Cerda 2009.

items.description: Run ConceptEvolve 'evolve' on the univalent Bloch constant problem to generate cross-domain concept cards
items.acceptance_criteria: Execute concept_evolve.py evolve with topic 'univalent Bloch constant tighter lower bound'. Verify results/concept_evolve/tree/ contains at least 8 concept folders, each with concept.json and README.md. Bridge graph JSON must exist with nodes and edges. At least 3 steering directions must be generated.
items.notes: Subagent delegation: researcher agent spawns concept_worker via concept_evolve

items.description: Map the hierarchy B <= B_l <= L <= B_u and catalog all known bounds for each constant
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase1/constants_hierarchy.md with a table listing all four constants (B, B_l, L, B_u), their definitions, best known lower bounds, best known upper bounds, conjectured values where applicable, and key references. Must include the chain of inequalities with proofs/citations for each link.

items.description: Implement numerical Koebe distortion bound evaluator for univalent functions in the class S
items.acceptance_criteria: Python script at results/phase2/koebe_distortion.py that: (a) computes the classical Koebe bounds |f(z)| >= |z|/(1+|z|)^2 and |f'(z)| >= (1-|z|)/(1+|z|)^3, (b) evaluates Skinner's refined B(|z|) function, (c) numerically solves for the implicit C(|z|) function from Skinner's theorem, (d) produces comparison plots saved to figures/koebe_bounds.png. All outputs verified against known values at |z| = 0, 0.5, 0.9.

items.description: Implement conformal mapping toolkit for extremal domain candidates
items.acceptance_criteria: Python module at results/phase2/conformal_toolkit.py providing: (a) Schwarz-Christoffel mapping for slit domains, (b) numerical conformal radius computation via Riemann mapping, (c) harmonic measure computation on simply connected domains, (d) unit tests for the disk and half-plane cases. Tests pass and conformal radii agree with known values to 6 decimal places.

items.description: Reproduce Skinner's B_u > 0.5708858 bound numerically from first principles
items.acceptance_criteria: Script at results/phase2/reproduce_skinner.py that: (a) implements the bootstrapping iteration from Skinner 2009, (b) converges to B_u > 0.5708858, (c) outputs iteration log showing convergence. The reproduced bound must match Skinner's published value to at least 5 decimal places. Document any discrepancies in results/phase2/reproduction_notes.md.

items.description: Build a numerical univalent disk radius estimator for parametric families of schlicht functions
items.acceptance_criteria: Module at results/phase2/univalent_disk.py that: (a) given a holomorphic univalent function f on D (represented via Taylor coefficients or a callable), computes B_f numerically via boundary analysis, (b) correctly returns B_f = 1 for f(z) = z, (c) correctly handles the Koebe function k(z) = z/(1-z)^2 (B_k = 1/4 for the normalized version), (d) handles at least 3 other test families. Runtime under 30 seconds per function evaluation.

items.description: Establish baseline metrics framework and comparison table against prior literature
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase2/baseline_metrics.md containing: (a) table of all published lower bounds for B_u with year, author, method, and bound value, (b) table of upper bounds, (c) gap analysis (current gap: 1 - 0.5708858 = 0.4291142), (d) identification of the most promising directions to tighten bounds based on Phase 1 analysis. Must reference at least 8 papers from sources.bib.

items.description: Run ConceptEvolve 'reframe' to identify cross-domain techniques applicable to tightening B_u bounds
items.acceptance_criteria: Execute concept_evolve.py reframe with problem 'tightening lower bound of univalent Bloch constant beyond 0.5708858'. Output must contain reframings in at least 8 domains (e.g., optimization, spectral theory, hyperbolic geometry, PDE, probability/Brownian motion, potential theory, algebraic geometry, numerical analysis). Each reframing must include a concrete technique mapping. Results stored in results/concept_evolve/.
items.notes: Subagent delegation: concept_worker explores cross-domain bridges

items.description: Develop improved bootstrapping iteration using sharper distortion estimates for subclasses of S
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase3/improved_bootstrap.py implementing: (a) at least 2 refinements to Skinner's bootstrapping method (e.g., using Bieberbach coefficient bounds, Grunsky inequalities, or hyperbolic derivative estimates), (b) each refinement must provably yield B(|z|) >= Skinner's B(|z|) for all |z| in (0,1), (c) the resulting lower bound for B_u must exceed 0.5708858 or a rigorous explanation of why the approach yields equal or weaker bounds. Mathematical justification in results/phase3/bootstrap_proof.md.

items.description: Investigate Landau's fixed-point approach (Kudryavtseva-Solodov style) for new B_u lower bounds
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase3/landau_approach.md analyzing: (a) how adding boundary fixed-point constraints to B[0] narrows the class and enlarges univalence domains, (b) whether the sharp invertibility domain results of Kudryavtseva-Solodov 2022 can be leveraged for B_u, (c) explicit computation for at least 2 specific fixed-point configurations, (d) a rigorous statement of whether this yields a new lower bound or not. If a new bound is obtained, it must be stated with proof sketch.

items.description: Explore hyperbolic metric and Schwarz-Pick refinement approach for univalent Bloch constant
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase3/hyperbolic_approach.md and supporting code results/phase3/hyperbolic_bounds.py. Must: (a) formulate B_u in terms of hyperbolic geometry of the image domain, (b) use the Schwarz-Pick lemma and its refinements (Beardon-Minda, Osserman) to derive growth/distortion bounds, (c) compute the resulting B_u lower bound numerically, (d) compare against Skinner's 0.5708858. If tighter, provide rigorous proof outline.

items.description: Run ConceptEvolve 'probe' on the specific bottleneck of Skinner's inequality chain
items.acceptance_criteria: Execute concept_evolve.py probe on 'slack in Skinner bootstrapping iteration for univalent Bloch constant - where does the iteration lose tightness'. Results must include: (a) identification of at least 2 specific bottleneck inequalities, (b) cross-domain bridge suggestions for each bottleneck, (c) anomaly analysis and validation checks. Stored in results/concept_evolve/.
items.notes: Subagent delegation: concept_worker deep-dives into bottleneck

items.description: Investigate variational/extremal-function approach: characterize near-extremal domains for B_u
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase3/extremal_domains.md and results/phase3/extremal_search.py. Must: (a) implement a numerical search over parametric families of schlicht functions (e.g., slit mappings, n-fold symmetric functions) to find functions with small B_f, (b) characterize geometric properties of near-extremal image domains (boundary structure, symmetry, number of slits), (c) evaluate B_f for at least 20 candidate functions, (d) identify the minimum B_f found and compare against B_u > 0.5708858. Figures of extremal domain candidates saved to figures/.

items.description: Develop novel approach combining Grunsky inequalities with univalent disk radius estimation
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase3/grunsky_approach.md documenting: (a) how Grunsky matrix eigenvalue bounds constrain the image geometry of f in S, (b) derivation of a lower bound on max disk radius in f(D) using Grunsky coefficients, (c) numerical evaluation for truncated Grunsky matrices of orders N=5,10,20, (d) resulting B_u lower bound compared to 0.5708858. If tighter, full proof sketch included.

items.description: Systematic numerical experiment: evaluate B_f across a comprehensive grid of schlicht functions
items.acceptance_criteria: Script at results/phase4/systematic_search.py that: (a) generates at least 500 schlicht functions from 5+ parametric families (Koebe rotations, slit mappings, convex functions, close-to-convex, starlike with various parameters), (b) computes B_f for each, (c) records results in results/phase4/Bf_table.csv, (d) produces histogram of B_f values (saved to figures/Bf_histogram.png), (e) identifies the function achieving minimum B_f. Runtime documentation included.

items.description: Convergence and sensitivity analysis of each proposed bound improvement
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase4/convergence_analysis.md with: (a) for each approach in Phase 3 (improved bootstrap, Landau, hyperbolic, Grunsky), document convergence behavior and parameter sensitivity, (b) plots of bound vs iteration/parameter for each method saved to figures/, (c) statistical summary of which approach yields the tightest bound, (d) error bars or rigorous bounds on numerical precision. At least 4 comparison plots.

items.description: Explore concept tree walks to identify unexplored research paths
items.acceptance_criteria: Execute concept_evolve.py walk with depth >= 3 on at least 2 seed concepts from the Phase 1 evolve run. Document results/phase4/concept_walks.md listing: (a) all paths explored, (b) at least 2 novel connections discovered between concepts, (c) assessment of whether any walk path suggests a genuinely new proof technique not yet tried. Reference specific concept folders in results/concept_evolve/tree/.
items.notes: Subagent delegation: concept-tree-explorer agent traverses concept folders

items.description: Head-to-head comparison of all Phase 3 approaches against Skinner's baseline
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase4/comparison_table.md with a single table containing: (a) method name, (b) resulting B_u lower bound (or 'no improvement'), (c) computational cost, (d) rigor level (fully rigorous / numerically supported / heuristic), (e) key insight, (f) reference to supporting code/proof. At least 4 rows (one per Phase 3 approach). Clearly state which approach(es) achieve a tighter bound than 0.5708858.

items.description: Attempt to construct a rigorous computer-assisted proof for any improved lower bound
items.acceptance_criteria: If any approach from Phase 3 yields a bound > 0.5708858: produce results/phase4/rigorous_bound.py implementing interval arithmetic verification (using mpmath or similar) that certifies the new bound. Output must include: (a) the certified bound value, (b) all intermediate computations with error tracking, (c) a log of the verification. If no improvement found, produce results/phase4/negative_results.md explaining exactly where each approach falls short and what further ideas remain.

items.description: Synthesize all findings into a comprehensive research report
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/report.md containing: (a) Abstract (150 words), (b) Introduction with problem statement and motivation, (c) Literature review citing at least 10 papers from sources.bib, (d) Methods section covering all approaches attempted, (e) Results section with key bounds and comparisons, (f) Discussion of what worked, what didn't, and why, (g) Conclusion with best achieved bound, (h) References. At least 3000 words total.

items.description: Generate publication-quality figures summarizing key results
items.acceptance_criteria: Figures directory contains at least 5 figures: (a) bound improvement timeline plot (historical B_u bounds vs year), (b) comparison bar chart of all attempted approaches, (c) convergence plot of best method, (d) near-extremal domain visualization, (e) concept tree visualization. All figures referenced in results/report.md.

items.description: Update sources.bib with all papers discovered during research and verify completeness
items.acceptance_criteria: sources.bib contains at least 15 complete BibTeX entries. Each entry has: author, title, journal/venue, year, DOI or arXiv ID where available. No duplicate entries. All papers cited in results/report.md appear in sources.bib. Run a consistency check script.

items.description: Mine citation graph of key papers using literature-graph-miner subagent for transferable ideas
items.acceptance_criteria: Using semantic_scholar graph command on Skinner 2009 (paper ID 4e70e76bcdcc5570677677ce2c4c5d333ce1ea09) and Carroll-Ortega-Cerda 2008 (paper ID a3c98ff25aff7e3f41e18f5de916ee99b9f39693), produce results/phase5/citation_graph.md listing: (a) papers citing both works, (b) common references, (c) at least 3 transferable ideas from adjacent fields, (d) any post-2020 developments found. Update sources.bib with newly discovered papers.
items.notes: Subagent delegation: literature-graph-miner agent mines citation networks

items.description: Peer review of main findings and bound claims
items.acceptance_criteria: Reviewer agent produces results/phase5/peer_review.md containing: (a) verification of all claimed bounds (do the proofs/computations check out?), (b) identification of any gaps in rigor, (c) suggestions for strengthening the weakest arguments, (d) overall assessment (accept/revise/reject) with detailed justification. Must check at least 3 specific mathematical claims from results/report.md.

items.description: Document open problems and future research directions emerging from this investigation
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase5/open_problems.md listing at least 5 concrete open problems or future directions, each with: (a) precise statement, (b) why it is promising, (c) estimated difficulty, (d) connection to this work. Must include at least one problem about upper bounds and one about computational methods.
